newsitem.title: UK: Russian fuel oil export figures show fall in April.
newsitem.headline: Russian fuel oil export figures show fall in April.

text.p: Russian exports of fuel oil from the Black Sea ports of Tuapse, Odessa and Novorossiisk and the Baltic port of Ventspils fell by 20 percent in April from March, shipping inspectors Petrak said on Thursday.
But the April total of 570,000 tonnes was still higher than January and February figures, suggesting March exports were unusually high.
Shipments of fuel oil from Tuapse, Odessa and Ventspils all fell, while Novorossiisk exported 209,730 tonnes, up from 187,767 tonnes.
The Petrak figures were broadly in line with those released on Wednesday by Petro Logistics, the Geneva-based consultancy, which surveys more outlets.
Petro Logistic figures said Baltic/Black Sea ports exported 1,050,000 tonnes of fuel oil in the first four weeks of April, down from the year's high of 1,412,000 in March.
Some fuel oil traders believe Russian refineries have been deterred from exporting in April by the poor prices their products have been fetching in European and Mediterranean markets.
But others believe Russian marketers are not so responsive to price falls and that technical and weather problems are more to blame for the drop in April figures.

Spring weather has now unfrozen the inland waterways in Russia, restarting the traditional summer fuel oil export season, which should bring an additional two million tonnes of product into Western markets, further pressuring prices. - London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
